description.purpose: The digest's shelf (GH #976): one row per finished digest -- {id, at, audience_set, title, items} -- beside its delivery, so the last digest can be read back by the round it was made for.
description.use_when: Written by ./shelf after every formatted digest; read by ./shelf on a read of the hive (in_read, op last).
description.not_in_scope: No search, no deletion: rows are kept, a read takes the newest.
description.emits_meaning: messages[]: one tool_result per operation. hop.operation/rows_affected for routing; SQL failures are normal tool_results with hop.error_code. hop.duration_ms is what that reply cost in milliseconds. A bundle reply (two or more tool_call turns, GH #295) stamps hop.operation 'bundle', sums hop.rows_affected over its legs and adds hop.bundle_errors: how many legs carry an error_code. That key is present on every bundle reply, 0 included, and never on a single-operation reply -- it is what an edge reads to see that one leg failed without opening the body, while hop.error_code keeps its hard meaning (the WHOLE reply is a refusal). results[]: the per-operation metadata of that same bundle reply, one entry per leg in call order -- {tool_call_id, operation, rows_affected, duration_ms} plus error_code if that one leg failed. It is a top-level body slot and not a key on the turn because a tool_result turn stays schema-pure ({origin, type, text, id}; ubf-body.json $defs/TurnObject is additionalProperties:false, so a metadata key there would dead-letter the whole reply), and tool_call_id is what ties an entry back to its turn. Like bundle_errors the slot exists only on a bundle reply -- a single-operation reply carries messages[] alone.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: tool_call turns with store-native args {operation, table, ...} from ./shelf; select names its columns.
examples: {operation: insert, table: digests, row: {id, at, audience_set, title, items}} -> tool_result, hop {operation: 'insert', rows_affected: 1}
